ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L561-1 through L561-50-1 and R561-1 through R561-40-1 of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier); Articles L561-45 through L561-49 CMF on the registre des bénéficiaires effectifs; Law No. 2016-1691 of 9 December 2016 (Sapin II); Code de commerce Articles L123-1 to L123-5-5 and R123-53 on RCS filing; EU Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843; Regulation (EU) 2018/1672 on cross-border cash controls.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: French law requires every company formation agent, accountant, notary, and legal representative to perform risk-based customer due diligence under CMF Article L561-5. Screening must cover all UBOs, directors, presidents, and authorized signatories against TRACFIN files, EU consolidated financial sanctions lists, UN Security Council sanctions, French national freezing measures including FCPG, and, where USD transactions or international trade are expected, OFAC SDN screening. PEP status is assessed under FATF/EU definitions; confirmed PEP status triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth verification, senior-management approval, and continuous monitoring. Failure to file and maintain the UBO declaration in the RNE is punishable under CMF Article L561-50 with criminal and administrative sanctions.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique électronique of INPI (https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) combined with the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE), INPI trademark database (data.inpi.fr), and Infogreffe (https://www.infogreffe.fr) for pre-filing availability checks.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French corporate names may be registered in a non-French language, but non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet for RCS/RNE purposes. Mandatory corporate documents, public notices, and filings must have a French version under Law No. 94-665 (loi Toubon). A French alias or descriptive subtitle is recommended to avoid registry refusal.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: French law does not provide a standalone pre-registration name reservation; the name is cleared at the moment of RCS filing through the Guichet unique and the commercial court registry. If the registry rejects the dénomination, the legal representative receives written reasons. The applicant may correct the name, add a distinguishing token, attach the trademark owner's written consent, and refile through the Guichet unique. Refusals based on public-order grounds or third-party rights may be submitted for judicial determination to the President of the competent Tribunal de commerce in référé; procedural refusals by the Guichet unique may be challenged before the administrative court. A fresh review period begins upon each corrected filing, and all French translations and authenticated governmental documents must be current, generally within 90 days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible through a registered domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) under Code de commerce Articles L123-10-3, L123-11-2, and R123-53, subject to a renewable limited term. No physical premises license is required for ISIC 4663 wholesale ocean-vessel distribution of hydraulic cement, but the French office must support real management substance: documents, correspondence, and accounting records must be available, and the president must be able to evidence administration at the address. A pure letterbox without local operational substance may attract challenge under Article 209B of the French General Tax Code and EU anti-avoidance rules.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate. For a standard wholesale cement distribution SAS with a compliant domiciliation address and transparent UBOs, unannounced on-site inspection risk is estimated at 10-15% annually. If the entity uses a virtual office, has fully non-resident management, or has a UBO or sanctions/PEP trigger, the probability increases to 25-35% per year.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce): Articles L. 123-1 to L. 123-9 (RCS registration and Extrait Kbis), L. 210-1 to L. 210-10 (general company provisions), L. 227-1 to L. 227-33 (Société par Actions Simplifiée constitution and corporate governance), R. 123-1 to R. 123-19 (registry filing procedure); supplemented by Law No. 2019-486 (PACTE Act), the Guichet unique implementing decree, and the Civil Code provisions on electronic signatures.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) maintaining the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) in the department of the registered office; all incorporation filings are submitted electronically through the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) single window at formalites.entreprises.data.gouv.fr.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de création d'entreprise (société) submitted via the mandatory Guichet unique electronic dossier, together with the signed Articles of Association (statuts constitutifs), the blocked-capital certificate, and the publication certificate; the operative registration is the inscription au Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés evidenced by the Extrait Kbis.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital for an SAS; the capital may be fixed at EUR 1. However, Article L. 227-3 of the Code de commerce requires that shares be fully paid up at subscription. Cash contributions must be deposited in a blocked bank account or with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations and may be released only after delivery of the Extrait Kbis; in-kind contributions must be appraised by a commissaire aux apports unless unanimously waived, where an individual contribution exceeds EUR 30,000 or the total value of in-kind contributions exceeds half of the share capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Articles of Association (statuts) filed with this board are approved and adopted without amendment; RESOLVED, that the founders subscribe to the share capital described in the subscription sheet, the shares being fully paid up; RESOLVED, that the registered office is fixed at the address recorded in the statuts, the Chairman being authorised to execute any lease; RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed Président with full powers to act and bind the Company; RESOLVED, that the Président is authorised to open the corporate bank account and to complete all registration formalities before the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés; RESOLVED, that every preliminary act performed in the Company's name is ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, execution and signature of the Articles of Association (statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporating shareholders; a notaire is required only where the statuts contain a transfer of real property or other notarial formalities; otherwise a private deed (acte sous seing privé) is valid.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the statuts containing all mandatory SAS clauses: denomination, form, registered office, corporate object, duration, share capital, contributions in cash or in kind, rights attached to shares, President's powers, share-transfer approval rules, corporate governance, audit thresholds, and fiscal year. Each shareholder must sign every page or use a compliant electronic signature (Article 1367 Civil Code); where in-kind contributions exceed statutory thresholds, appoint a commissaire aux apports before final execution.
required_dossiers: SAS Articles of Association executed by all shareholders
Subscription sheet and allocation of shares table
Valuation report of the commissaire aux apports, if applicable
Identity documents of each shareholder and the President
Sworn declaration of non-condemnation and legal capacity of the President
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries an irregular clause or missing mandatory mention, the shareholders adopt a corrective resolution and sign a supplementary deed (acte rectificatif) which is filed with the RCS before final inscription.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of paid-up capital and issuance of blocked-funds certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any French or EU/EEA bank, or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC); the bank acts as depositary and issues the attestation de blocage de fonds.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional account in the name of the company en formation. Deposit 100% of the cash share capital subscribed. The depositary issues a blocked-funds certificate stating the amount held and the names of the subscribing shareholders. The certificate must expressly confirm that the funds may not be released until the Extrait Kbis is produced and presented.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association
Subscription sheet showing individual cash subscriptions
Identity documents of the signatories authorized to open the provisional account
Deposit order signed by all shareholders or their agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses a non-resident signatory or identifies an enhanced compliance issue, appoint a French-resident co-signatory or substitute the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations as depositary; obtain a corrected attestation if the initial certificate is defective.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the incorporation notice in a legal announcements newspaper
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: An approved Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) published in the department in which the registered office is situated.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Insert an avis de constitution containing the company name, legal form SAS, share capital, registered office address, corporate object, the name of the President, and the RCS filing place. The JAL editor verifies the legal mentions and issues an attestation de parution, which must be filed with the incorporation dossier.
required_dossiers: Signed Articles of Association
Identity details of the President and shareholders
Notice text approved by the shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL editor rejects the draft due to incomplete compulsory mentions, correct and republish the notice promptly; the new attestation de parution supersedes the earlier version for submission to the RCS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing of the incorporation dossier with the Guichet unique for RCS registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) operating the single window (formalites.entreprises.data.gouv.fr), transmitting the dossier to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce for inscription au Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the electronic déclaration de création and attach the signed statuts, blocked-capital certificate, JAL publication certificate, identity documents, the Declaration of Beneficial Owners (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs), and any powers of attorney. Pay the applicable registry fee online. After verification, the RCS enters the company and issues the Extrait Kbis, SIREN, SIRET and APE/NAF code.
required_dossiers: Executed Articles of Association in PDF
Attestation de blocage de fonds from the bank or CDC
Journal d'Annonces Légales publication certificate
Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs (DBE)
Identity documents and proof of residential address for the President
Sworn statements of non-condemnation and capacity
Power of attorney, if filing through an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the INPI or Greffe issues a notice of incompleteness, upload the missing or corrected documents within the fifteen-day procedural window; where foreign documents are submitted, supply certified French translations (traduction assermentée); a refusal may be challenged before the President of the Commercial Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration settlement: Kbis extraction, statutory books and fiscal and social registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce for Kbis; Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) for tax identifiers and IS/VAT registration; URSSAF and the employment authorities for social registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the Extrait Kbis, present it to the depositary bank to release the blocked funds. Order the share-register (registre des mouvements de titres) and minute books for shareholders' and board decisions. Complete the DGFiP formalities to obtain the SIRET-linked tax regime elections and VAT number, and register as an employer with URSSAF if hiring will commence.
required_dossiers: Extrait Kbis
Registered office lease or Certificate of domiciliation
Blocked-funds certificate presented to the bank for release
Identity file of the President and any directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If fiscal or social identifiers are delayed, the Kbis serves as prima facie proof of existence for interim operations; any material error in the Kbis, SIREN or NAF code is corrected by a rectification request (requête en rectification) addressed directly to the greffe.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) and the Préfecture du département; jurisdiction is triggered only if fixed bulk-storage silos, transhipment stations or mechanical processing installations are established. Pure wholesale distribution of Portland clinker does not require an industrial manufacturing permit.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required for pure wholesale trading under ISIC 4663; optional operational authorizations include a port concession agreement or temporary occupation authorization (autorisation d'occupation du domaine public portuaire) for dock-side unloading, an Authorised Economic Operator (AEO) customs certificate for simplified import procedures, and a town-planning permission for any commercial warehouse footprint.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL), acting under the Ministry of Ecological Transition; the Préfet de département is the decision authority for installations classées pour la protection de l'environnement (ICPE).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full Environmental Impact Assessment for pure wholesale distribution without fixed installations. If the operator installs storage silos or a mineral transhipment station, the facility will fall under the ICPE nomenclature (Rubriques 2515/2516) and require either declaration (déclaration) or registration (enregistrement), or authorization (autorisation) above mechanical-power or storage-volume thresholds; DREAL confirms the applicable class at the project-design stage.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Pure distribution generates no process wastewater; any stormwater drainage and runoff from loading or silo areas must meet ICPE generic discharge limits, including pH 5.5-8.5, suspended solids not exceeding 35 mg/L, total hydrocarbons not exceeding 15 mg/L, and oil-film-free effluent. Fugitive dust at transfer points must be controlled by sealed conveyors, telescopic loading chutes and filtration systems to maintain ambient occupational limits: inhalable dust not exceeding 10 mg/m3 TWA and respirable dust not exceeding 4 mg/m3 TWA under Articles R. 4222-10 and R. 4222-12 of the French Labor Code. Noise output at the nearest sensitive facade must respect the ICPE emergence standards of 5 dB(A) by day and 3 dB(A) by night.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Workplace opening declaration (déclaration d'ouverture d'un établissement) under the Labor Code; fire-safety certification and evacuation arrangements reviewed by the service départemental d'incendie et de secours (SDIS) where the premises receive personnel; structural load inspection reports for silos, gantries and truck-loading platforms issued by an approved technical control bureau (Apave, Bureau Veritas, DEKRA, Socotec or equivalent); dust-hazard management plans for bulk handling points; and, where the workforce exceeds 50 employees, creation of the Comité Social et Économique (CSE). All premises must meet building-code accessibility and electrical-safety standards before operational clearance is granted.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle et numérique; taxpayer portal: impots.gouv.fr; company/registration portal: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (Guichet unique); customs interface: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) with DELTA/PRO.DOUANE; VAT number verification: VIES (europa.eu/vies).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned SAS is incorporated online at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; INSEE issues SIREN/SIRET; the local Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) assigns the VAT identification number (numéro d'identification TVA) and the EORI number is obtained from DGDDI for customs filing of bulk-clinker exports. A non-EU seller without a French establishment that becomes liable for French VAT must register through the SIE and appoint an accredited fiscal representative (représentant fiscal) before invoicing; intra-EU acquisition checks require a valid VIES-validated VAT number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Under Art. 239 bis AA CGI, an eligible newly-created SAS may elect (before the end of its first fiscal year) to be taxed on a pass-through basis for up to five years; a French parent SAS may elect fiscal integration (Art. 223 A CGI) for 95%+ owned French subsidiaries; the mère-fille participation regime is available; no US-style check-the-box classification exists in France — entity tainting follows the commercial form, the statut de lieu de direction, and ATAD 2 anti-hybrid rules (Art. 209, 212 bis CGI).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée – TVA), Code Général des Impôts (CGI), Articles 256–257; customs duties and import VAT administered by DGDDI at importation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Domestic franchise en base de TVA exemption for small established suppliers of goods below EUR 85,000 annual turnover (tolerance EUR 93,500), reduced by the 2025 Finance Act; non-established foreign suppliers have no franchise — VAT registration is compulsory for any taxable supply made in France and for all intra-EU acquisitions above EUR 10,000 (OSS distance-sales threshold); import VAT is due on every physical importation of portland clinker into France.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing for domestic B2B supplies phased-in: large/mid-size enterprises from 1 September 2026, SMEs/micro from 1 September 2027; invoices must be sent through a registered Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP) using structured Factur-X, UBL or CII formats; e-reporting of transaction and payment data flows to the DGFiP via the PDP/API network; no per-invoice 'fiscal stamp' or Italian-style SDI real-time clearance; cross-border/export transactions are covered by e-reporting; retail cash-register software must be certified under the 2018 anti-fraud law.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of bulk portland clinker/cement to non-EU destinations are exempt from French VAT (Art. 262-I-1° CGI) where the supplier proves that the goods left the EU under an accepted electronic export declaration (E-DAU/ECS exit confirmation) within the statutory proof window (normally 90 days from the taxable event, flexibly extended for long-haul bulk maritime voyages); the buyer must be a non-taxable/third-country party or the supply must qualify as an exempt intra-Community dispatch (Art. 262 ter CGI) with a VIES-validated customer VAT number.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration: Déclaration Administrative Unique (DAU/E-DAU) filed in the DGDDI DELTA/PRO.DOUANE system with accepted exit-confinement confirmation for the non-EU port of discharge
Bill of Lading: full set of original or authorised sea waybill/telex-release B/L evidencing bulk clinker laden on the named ocean vessel and destined for a third-country port

Inward Remittance Certificate: bank/SWIFT advice (MT103 or LC settlement) evidencing receipt of the export proceeds in EUR against the invoice, cross-referenced with the Banque de France balance-of-payments filing

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, acting within the Eurosystem, together with the French Ministry for the Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty and the Directorate-General of Customs and Indirect Taxes for applicable trade, statistical, and cash-reporting controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro, which is fully convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions. A French SAS may generally receive foreign currency, convert funds, pay foreign suppliers, remit dividends, repay shareholder or bank debt, and make cross-border investments without a general foreign-exchange approval or mandatory conversion into euros. Transfers remain subject to bank anti-money-laundering, sanctions, beneficial-ownership, tax, accounting, and payment-screening controls. Dividend and interest remittances must be supported by valid corporate approvals, distributable profits or a legally valid financing basis, withholding-tax analysis, treaty documentation where relevant, and evidence that the transaction is not a disguised distribution or unlawful return of capital. Cross-border payments may also trigger statistical reporting, VAT, customs, Intrastat, balance-of-payments, or tax-reporting obligations depending on the transaction and counterparty.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement and no general mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. Export proceeds may be retained in foreign-currency accounts or converted at the company's discretion, subject to ordinary accounting, tax, customs, sanctions, AML, and bank reporting requirements. There is no general French deadline requiring export receipts to be repatriated or converted. Banks may request commercial invoices, transport documents, customs declarations, contracts, and proof of economic purpose before crediting or transferring funds. Cash physically transported across the European Union external border at or above EUR 10,000, or its equivalent, is subject to applicable EU and French customs declaration rules. Unusual payment patterns, third-party settlements, over-invoicing, unexplained prepayments, or transactions involving sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions may be delayed, rejected, or reported to TRACFIN.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. and the relevant Crédit Agricole regional bank
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; optional foreign-currency collection account; capital escrow account where required for a specific incorporation or capital-increase process
Operational Account; optional foreign-currency collection account; capital escrow account where required for a specific incorporation or capital-increase process

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payment accounts and collections, low as a sole treasury bank. An electronic-money institution or payment institution authorised in France or another EEA state may provide payment services in France under applicable authorisation and passporting rules, subject to safeguarding, AML, sanctions, account-usage, and transaction-monitoring controls. An EMI account is not a bank deposit and generally does not provide deposit-guarantee protection. An offshore non-EEA digital EMI cannot lawfully provide regulated payment services into France solely through an offshore platform without an applicable French or EEA authorisation, branch, agent, or other lawful market-access basis. Fintechs may impose limits on bulk payments, trade finance, cash deposits, sanctioned jurisdictions, commodity trades, third-party receipts, and high-value international wires. A regulated French or EEA bank should remain the primary account for capital injections, payroll, taxes, customs, letters of credit, and material supplier settlements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal rule requiring all directors to appear physically at a branch for corporate-account opening. Remote onboarding may be permitted where the institution can complete reliable identification, beneficial-owner verification, powers-of-attorney validation, source-of-funds review, and electronic-signature controls. In practice, banks may require a live video interview, certified or apostilled corporate documents, an in-person meeting, a French-resident representative, or branch attendance for non-resident shareholders, complex ownership chains, higher-risk jurisdictions, cash-intensive activity, unusual commodity flows, or unresolved identity issues. The legal representative and each beneficial owner should be prepared to complete bank-specific verification; a proxy cannot eliminate ultimate-beneficial-owner diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder, director, or ultimate beneficial owner with no established French operating footprint
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current articles of association; Kbis or registration extract; shareholder register and ownership chart through all intermediate entities; certified identity and address documents for directors and beneficial owners; tax-residence certificates; board or shareholder appointment resolutions; French business plan; premises or registered-office evidence; customer and supplier contracts; projected transaction flows; explanation of French commercial substance and management arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear beneficial ownership, nominee arrangements, bearer-like ownership, or ownership chain involving multiple jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal-entity ownership chart; constitutional documents for every holding entity; registers of shareholders and directors; certificates of incumbency or good standing; trust or foundation documents where applicable; notarised or certified powers of attorney; beneficial-owner declarations; documentary explanation of control rights; sanctions and politically exposed person screening results.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bulk trade in cement, clinker, or construction materials with high-value cross-border payments and limited transaction history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed product description and HS classification; supplier and customer contracts; purchase orders; commercial invoices; bills of lading; certificates of origin and quality; customs declarations; vessel and port information; Incoterms; insurance documents; freight agreements; margin model; expected monthly volumes and values; counterparty screening; evidence of end-use and delivery locations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving third-party payers, unrelated beneficiaries, payment agents, or accounts in jurisdictions not matching the contracting party
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tri-party agreement or documented agency mandate; board approval; invoice and underlying contract; explanation of the payment chain; proof of agency or financing relationship; beneficial-owner and sanctions screening for all parties; written confirmation from the contracting counterparty; bank-approved payment instructions; reconciliation controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large shareholder loan, capital contribution, intercompany transfer, or inbound payment with an unclear purpose code
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed loan or contribution agreement; corporate approvals; funding-source evidence; lender and borrower ownership information; transfer-pricing analysis where relevant; repayment schedule; interest terms; tax and withholding analysis; bank transfer instructions; accounting entries; proof that the funds are not proceeds of crime or an unlawful distribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk country exposure, sanctioned-party proximity, politically exposed person, adverse media, or vessel and port sanctions risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty identification package; sanctions screening logs covering entities, owners, directors, vessels, ports, banks, and goods; PEP and adverse-media results; end-use and end-user certification; route and vessel history; contractual sanctions clauses; export-control review; legal opinion or compliance memorandum; enhanced monitoring plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent projected turnover, unexplained cash activity, rapid pass-through of funds, or account activity inconsistent with wholesale distribution
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12-to-24-month cash-flow forecast; management accounts; audited accounts or opening balance sheet; tax registrations; payroll and expense forecast; inventory and working-capital model; customer concentration analysis; treasury policy; expected payment calendar; reconciliation procedure; explanation of seasonality and one-off transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete French registration, missing beneficial-owner filing, address mismatch, or expired corporate documents
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Recent Kbis extract; updated SIREN and SIRET information; beneficial-owner filing evidence; registered-office agreement; current articles; appointment and delegation documents; tax and VAT registration evidence; certified translations where requested; formal explanation and remediation timeline for any discrepancy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Request for an account before completion of incorporation or before capital is legally available for use
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Draft articles; incorporation resolution; shareholder identity package; subscription forms; source-of-funds evidence; capital deposit instructions; certificate of deposit process; post-registration Kbis delivery commitment; segregated capital-account mandate; evidence that capital funds will not be used operationally before release.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route paid-in capital through a French bank capital account or another bank-approved account structure designated for the incorporation or capital increase, using a transfer reference that identifies the subscriber, the SAS, and the capital contribution. Provide the executed subscription documentation, corporate approvals, source-of-funds evidence, ownership information, and bank-requested purpose description. After registration or the relevant capital-increase formalities, obtain the bank's release confirmation and transfer funds to the operational account. Shareholder loans, intercompany funding, and additional paid-in capital should be supported by separate agreements and accounting classifications. Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro-denominated EEA payments where available; use SWIFT for non-SEPA currencies or jurisdictions. Preserve MT103 or equivalent payment confirmations, remitter and beneficiary details, UETR, invoice or agreement references, and reconciliation evidence. Do not route capital through personal accounts, unrelated third parties, anonymous payment services, or unapproved offshore wallets.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer for eligible euro supplier payments and SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA or foreign-currency payments. For new, high-value, or higher-risk suppliers, use an irrevocable documentary commercial letter of credit issued or confirmed by a regulated bank, with compliant presentation of commercial invoices, bills of lading, certificates of origin, insurance documents, inspection certificates, and other stipulated documents. Documentary collections may be used where the counterparty and jurisdiction are sufficiently established. Payment instructions must match the legal contracting party, verified bank account, invoice, goods, Incoterms, vessel, port, and customs documentation. Apply dual approval, callback verification for changed bank details, sanctions screening, segregation of duties, payment-limit controls, and three-way matching between purchase order, receipt or shipping evidence, and invoice. Record foreign-exchange rates, fees, value dates, hedging allocations, VAT and customs references, and the accounting treatment of each settlement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/foreign-currency forwards with an authorised bank or eligible regulated investment firm, limited to documented forecast or contracted commercial exposures and subject to MiFID II, EMIR, suitability or appropriateness, collateral, confirmation, and reporting requirements where applicable.

Foreign-exchange swaps for short-term liquidity and settlement management, provided the transaction is documented, proportionate to the underlying exposure, and entered into with an authorised counterparty under appropriate master documentation.
Currency swaps for longer-term financing or recurring currency mismatches, subject to counterparty credit limits, valuation, collateral, accounting, EMIR, and board-approved treasury-policy controls.

Non-deliverable forwards only for currencies and counterparties for which the instrument is legally available and economically appropriate; settlement is generally in an agreed currency without delivery of the restricted currency. NDFs may be subject to MiFID II, EMIR, benchmark, margin, clearing, reporting, and product-governance rules and should not be used to evade foreign-exchange controls.

Plain-vanilla currency options or collars may be used for documented commercial exposures where the bank confirms product eligibility, pricing, appropriateness, accounting, and disclosure requirements.
No speculative proprietary FX trading, leveraged derivatives without documented exposure, or transactions with unregulated counterparties should be permitted under the operating treasury policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts and allocation of profit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders or sole shareholder of the SAS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Potential court injunction and daily coercive penalty; directors may incur civil liability for failure to convene or approve accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing, including balance sheet, income statement, notes and applicable management report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French commercial court registry through the INPI Guichet Unique
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval, or within two months after approval when filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction and potential fine of approximately EUR 1,500, increasing to approximately EUR 3,000 for repeated non-compliance; persistent registry non-compliance may contribute to administrative removal proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return Form 2065 and annual tax package
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally by the second working day after 1 May for a financial year ending on 31 December; otherwise within three months after year-end, subject to the applicable electronic filing calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge generally 10% of tax due, plus late-payment interest generally 0.20% per month; increased penalties may apply for tax evasion or repeated non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual CFE payment or exemption review
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally payable by 15 December; advance payment may be due by 15 June where the applicable CFE threshold is met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment surcharge generally 5% plus late-payment interest generally 0.20% per month; collection enforcement may follow.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership and shareholder information review
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: INPI Beneficial Ownership Register and French commercial registry, where a filing is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No annual confirmation filing is generally required; changes must generally be reported within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or inaccurate filing may result in court injunctions, criminal penalties for responsible individuals, and restrictions or registry consequences affecting the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate records and statutory register review
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate governance function; documents remain available at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least annually, preferably before approval of annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No standalone filing fee; inaccurate or incomplete records may create director liability, evidentiary risk, and penalties for related statutory breaches.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally mandatory for an SAS exceeding at least two of three thresholds at the relevant assessment date: EUR 5 million balance-sheet total, EUR 10 million turnover excluding tax, and 50 average employees. Additional mandatory appointment rules may apply to certain parent, subsidiary, or controlled-group structures. Voluntary appointment is permitted.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the French Accounting Standards Authority (ANC) regulations for statutory individual accounts. IFRS may apply to consolidated accounts where legally permitted or required.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not generally require an annual UBO confirmation filing. The company must conduct an annual internal verification, maintain accurate shareholder and control information, record share transfers in the share movement register and shareholder accounts, and file UBO changes generally within 30 days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Share movement register and individual shareholder accounts
Corporate decision and shareholder minutes book
Register of directors or corporate officers, where maintained or required by the company's governance documents
Supporting documentation for beneficial ownership determinations

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 600-1,800 per year, approximately USD 650-1,950, depending on address, mail handling, document scanning, and corporate secretarial services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately EUR 3,000-10,000 per year, or USD 3,250-10,900, for a small-to-medium SAS with routine operations; complex or group audits may exceed this range

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% for fiscal years opened on or after 1 January 2024 (standard rate, CGI art. 219-I-a)
